{{Quote|Brave talk. But the Council&mdash;''and'' the Empire will survive.|Carnor Jax|<ref name="CE6">[[Crimson Empire 6|''Crimson Empire'' 6]]</ref>}}
The '''Imperial Ruling Council''', also known as the '''High Council''' and as the '''Emperor's Inner Circle''', was a collective body of [[Imperial Advisor/Legends|advisors]] led by [[Grand Vizier/Legends|Grand Vizier]] [[Sate Pestage/Legends|Sate Pestage]] that constituted the effective leadership of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]]. While [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] was [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]], the Council managed the daily affairs of the Empire and carried out the Emperor's will.

Following the [[Emperor/Legends|Emperor's]] [[Death/Legends|death]] at the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]], Pestage took his throne as regent while other Councilors formed a tribunal known as the '''Emperor's Ruling Circle''' or '''Cabal''' in opposition, and ruled the Empire after the fall of Pestage and his successor, [[Director of Imperial Intelligence]] [[Ysanne Isard]]. The [[Battle of Onderon (Galactic Civil War)|final death]] of a [[Cloning/Legends|reborn]] Palpatine was orchestrated by a group of conspirators who seized power as the '''Imperial Interim Ruling Council''', but fell to internal conflicts and the depredations of Imperial loyalists.

==History==
===Evolution up to the Battle of Endor===
[[File:Palpatine_Sets_Army_Vote_Date.png|thumb|left|250px|The Ruling Council had its basis in Palpatine's early circle of advisors, such as Mas Amedda and Sly Moore.]]

In [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]],<ref name="NEC" /> [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] [[Declaration of a New Order|transformed]] the Republic into the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]].<ref name="ROTS">{{Film|III}}</ref> Early in his reign as [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Galactic Emperor]], Palpatine's inner circle joined him to receive reports given by [[Imperial Military/Legends|Imperial military]] advisors, and included [[Mas Amedda/Legends|Mas Amedda]] and [[Sly Moore/Legends|Sly Moore]], who served him as [[Emperor/Legends|Emperor]]<ref name="DLRODV">''[[Dark Lord: The Rise of Darth Vader]]''</ref> as they had when he was Chancellor.<ref name="AOTC">{{Film|II}}</ref> Shortly after the birth of the Empire, the inner circle established the [[Imperial Security Bureau/Legends|Imperial Security Bureau]], an intelligence agency created to rival the newly-reorganized [[Imperial Intelligence/Legends|Imperial Intelligence]].<ref name="FUCG">''[[The Force Unleashed Campaign Guide]]''</ref>

Under the [[New Order/Legends|New Order]] of the Galactic Empire, the Imperial Ruling Council was formed, with old allies of Palpatine's among its appointees, such as ousted [[Chommell sector/Legends|Chommell sector]] senator [[Janus Greejatus/Legends|Janus Greejatus]]<ref name="JG">{{DB|character|janusgreejatus|Greejatus, Janus}}</ref> and covert [[Emperor's Hand/Legends|Emperor's Hand]] [[Sarcev Quest]], the first<ref name="EP" /> of many of Palpatine's subordinates in the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]] of [[The Force/Legends|the Force]] to be initiated into the Council.<ref name="DESB">''[[Dark Empire Sourcebook]]''</ref> The Ruling Council's head, [[Grand Vizier/Legends|Grand Vizier]] [[Sate Pestage/Legends|Sate Pestage]],<ref name="EGW" /> had taken taken over many of the Empire's daily operations prior to the [[Battle of Hoth/Legends|Battle of Hoth]]<ref name="DESB" /> in [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]].<ref name="NEC" />

By [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]],<ref name="NEC" /> the time of the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]], the [[Minister/Legends|ministers]] and [[Governor/Legends|governors]] nearest the Emperor had come to be known as the Emperor's Inner Circle,<ref name="GSWU2">''[[A Guide to the Star Wars Universe, Second Edition, Revised and Expanded]]''</ref> a cadre of [[Imperial Advisor/Legends|Imperial Advisors]] that included Pestage, Greejatus, [[Sim Aloo/Legends|Sim Aloo]], [[Kren Blista-Vanee/Legends|Kren Blista-Vanee]], and [[Ars Dangor/Legends|Ars Dangor]],<ref name="AJC">{{SWArchive|url=community/askjc/jocasta/askjc20030602.html|text=Ask the Lucasfilm Jedi Council: Who are the gentlemen with the Emperor?}}</ref> an ally from Palpatine's time as a [[Senator/Legends|senator]].<ref name="DSTC">''[[Death Star Technical Companion]]''</ref>

[[File:EmperorsArrival-SWHC10.png|thumb|right|250px|The Emperor's Ruling Circle among Palpatine's retinue on the second Death Star]]
Members of the Emperor's Inner Circle,<ref name="AJC" /> Greejatus,<ref name="JG" /> Aloo,<ref name="SA">{{Topps|set=2014 Topps Star Wars Chrome Perspectives|cardname=Sim Aloo|link=https://www.tcdb.com/ViewCard.cfm/sid/95707/cid/6711488/2014-Topps-Star-Wars-Chrome-Perspectives-40E-Sim-Aloo}}</ref> and Blista-Vanee among them,<ref name="KBV">{{Topps|set=2013 Topps Star Wars Galactic Files Series 2|cardname=Kren Blista-Vanee|link=https://www.tcdb.com/ViewCard.cfm/sid/93283/cid/6569552/2013-Topps-Star-Wars-Galactic-Files-Series-2-526-Kren-Blista-Vanee}}</ref> accompanied their master as his [[Lambda-class T-4a shuttle/Legends|shuttle]] arrived aboard the [[Death Star/Legends|second Death Star]] to spring the trap set for the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] over [[Endor/Legends|Endor]]. However, the Emperor was betrayed and [[Death/Legends|slain]] by his [[Sith apprentice/Legends|apprentice]], [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]],<ref name="ROTJn">[[Star Wars: Return of the Jedi (novelization)|''Star Wars'' Episode VI: ''Return of the Jedi'' novelization]]</ref> and all six advisors soon followed when the Rebellion succeeded in destroying the [[Space station/Legends|space station]].<ref name="SA" />

===After Endor: Sate Pestage and the Cabal===
{{Quote|Haste and treason seldom combine well&hellip; I would have Imperial Intelligence arrest these fools, but Isard is using them to get to me. I know it.|[[Sate Pestage/Legends|Sate Pestage]]|<ref name="RS28">[[X-Wing Rogue Squadron 28|''X-Wing Rogue Squadron'' 28]]</ref>}}
[[File:Pestage_Tribunal.jpg|thumb|left|250px|The death of Palpatine split the Council between Grand Vizier Sate Pestage and the Emperor's Ruling Circle.]]

Though no clear succession plan had been left by Palpatine in the event of his death, Sate Pestage held the best claim to rule, and took control of the Empire as regent.<ref name="EGW" /> However, lacking his predecessor's charisma and influence, the Grand Vizier was vulnerable to domestic rivals, chief among them a tribunal formed by the fallen Emperor's advisors known as the Ruling Circle,<ref name="NEC" /> though Pestage labeled them "the Cabal".<ref name="RS21">[[X-Wing Rogue Squadron 21|''X-Wing Rogue Squadron'' 21]]</ref>

Based on Coruscant and led by Ars Dangor, the Emperor's Ruling Circle recalled the Empire's remaining forces to be redeployed in defense of so-called [[Fortress world/Legends|fortress worlds]],<ref name="CTD" /> [[Planet/Legends|planets]] nearly as well-defended as the capital of Coruscant<ref name="BDC3">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/sw20050421planet3|series=Byss and the Deep Core|text=Part 3: Prakith}}</ref> in inner [[Star system/Legends|star systems]] of particular strategic or economic significance, fearing an invasion of the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]] by the Rebellion-turned-[[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]]. However, though they feigned continued loyalty to the Empire,<ref name="EA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> prominent figures such as [[Grand Moff/Legends|Grand Moff]] [[Ardus Kaine]] of [[Oversector Outer]]<ref name="EGW" /> and [[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Zsinj]] of [[Quelii Oversector]] ignored the regency's requests, preferring to cement their own powerbases than see their assets divided among the interests of the Ruling Circle.<ref name="CTD" /> The Ruling Council's ability to command and redirect the Empire's remaining fleets was further disrupted by Rebel agents who sabotaged and destroyed several key [[HoloNet/Legends|HoloNet]] installations that transmitted orders from Coruscant to Imperial commanders around the galaxy.<ref name=":0">"[[Recon & Report: The Journey to Coruscant]]" — [[Star Wars Adventure Journal 2|''Star Wars Adventure Journal'' 2]] <small>(reprinted in [[The Best of the Star Wars Adventure Journal, Issues 1-4|''The Best of the Star Wars Adventure Journal'', Issues 1-4]])</small></ref> By [[6 ABY/Legends|two years after]] the Battle of Endor, the Imperial rulers, too preoccupied with internal power struggles to provide effective tactical guidance, had placed the fleet elements responsible for the defense of the Core under the command of Admiral<ref name="KC">{{JournalCite|7|The Kaal Connection}}</ref> [[Uther Kermen]].<ref name="EGW" /> In the six months since the Battle of Endor, the Ruling Council was able to redeploy around half of the Empire's remaining naval forces to defend key systems throughout the Core Worlds. Most of these systems consisted of vital [[Starship/Legends|starship]] repair and [[Shipyard/Legends|construction centers]] like [[Corellia/Legends|Corellia]] and [[Kuat/Legends|Kuat]], heavy industry worlds like [[Kelada/Legends|Kelada]], and productive [[Agriworld/Legends|agriculture worlds]] like [[Salliche/Legends|Salliche]].<ref name=":0" />

The Ruling Council was concerned that their power would evaporate if the Empire lost its ability to construct and repair the navy's starships, and thus viewed [[Kuat Drive Yards/Legends|Kuat Drive Yards]] and the [[Corellian Engineering Corporation/Legends|Corellian Engineering Corporation]] as targets of imminent assault by the New Republic. They abandoned [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|rimward]] shipyards like the [[Sluis Van Shipyards|stardocks]] at [[Sluis Van/Legends|Sluis Van]] in favor of facilities closer to the Core. They redeployed at least fifteen [[Imperial-class Star Destroyer/Legends|Imperial Star Destroyers]] to supplement the defense of the the [[Kuat system/Legends|Kuat system]], twenty-five to the [[Corellian system/Legends|Corellian system]], and anywhere from two to five Destroyers to other shipyard facilities throughout the Core sectors. [[Grand Admiral/Legends|Grand Admiral]] [[Josef Grunger]] and his [[Super Star Destroyer/Legends|Super Star Destroyer]] ''[[Aggressor (Executor-class)|Aggressor]]'' were recalled to help defend the [[CEC shipyards|Corellian shipyards]], but he instead went rogue and planned to use the Corellian system as a staging point for an assault against Coruscant. While Imperial control on the planets themselves loosened, every starship facility faced extreme security crackdowns. Any workers with questionable loyalties were imprisoned and replaced by Imperial Navy technical personnel. Patrols were given rotating schedules, and every ship entering and leaving the systems were thoroughly searched. To prevent the shipyards from falling into New Republic hands, every stardock and ship under construction at Kuat and Corellia were rigged to blow with explosives if their respective defense fleet commanders issued orders to scuttle the shipyards.<ref name=":0" /> 

Another of the Ruling Council's concerns was losing [[Arakyd Industries/Legends|Arakyd's]] giant assembly factory on Kelada. This facility was a major producer of [[Repulsorlift/Legends|repulsorlift]] and [[Walker/Legends|walker]] components, and assembled [[74-Z speeder bike/Legends|speeder bikes]] and other [[Repulsorcraft/Legends|repulsorcrafts]]. A contingent of ten Star Destroyers were deployed to patrol the system, and the planet was fortified with a [[V-150 Planet Defender/Legends|KDY v-150 Planet Defender]] and a [[Planetary shield/Legends|planetary shield]]. Stormtroopers were added to the starport's security forces, and customs officers cracked down on all regulations to prevent infiltration by saboteurs. The Council knew they couldn't possibly control the galaxy using their shrinking fleet, and increased the production of repulsorlift and walker systems dramatically. Imperial Army equipment was given a priority to maintain ground-based control of less vital worlds. To meet this demand, new factories were constructed on Kelada. The Ruling Council abandoned many industrial worlds in favor of ones closer to the Core. Imperial engineers dismantled their factories and shipped major components and raw materials towards the Core to build new factories like the ones on Kelada.<ref name=":0" /> 

Besides fortifying systems that provided military might in starships and war machines, the Ruling Council improved security on key agricultural worlds. Fertile worlds nearest Coruscant came under greater military scrutiny than ever before, with Salliche receiving the most attention. Salliche was home to [[Salliche Agricultural Corporation|Salliche Ag Corporation]], which administered agricultural plants throughout the Core Worlds. The Council disbanded [[Legislature (Salliche)|Salliche's governing body]] and placed the the system under the command of [[Moff/Legends|Moff]] [[Gegren Throsen]]. His senior staff replaced bureaucrats, while stormtroopers replaced corporate troops. The equivalent of an Imperial garrison and two Star Destroyers were sent to each of the eighteen worlds under the control of the Salliche Ag Corporation. Throsen's hasty and unexpected takeover caused workers, bureaucrats, and corporate soldiers, instigated by Rebel cells, to openly revolt against the Council's increasing control. Several New Republic agents worked to stir an all-out rebellion and disrupt the distribution of food around the Core.<ref name=":0" />

Amid the looming threat of a New Republic invasion of the Core and possibly Coruscant, the Ruling Council enacted a plan initially devised by Sate Pestage to hold [[Chandrila/Legends|Chandrila]] hostage. Despite not being a strategic world, seven Imperial Star Destroyers were deployed to blockade Chandrila. All ground troops were withdrawn and all Imperial facilities were cleared out and abandoned. In the event the New Republic moved against Coruscant, the Ruling Council planned to [[Orbital bombardment/Legends|bombard]] Chandrila.<ref name=":0" />     

An unsuccessful attempt to seize control over the Empire by the Inner Circle<ref name="GSWU2" /> of the Imperial Ruling Council was thwarted by Palpatine's former agent Sarcev Quest,<ref name="EP" /> but the conflict between the Grand Vizier and the Council was carefully cultivated by [[Director of Imperial Intelligence]] [[Ysanne Isard]]. She regarded Pestage and the Council alike as incompetents who had to be removed to ensure the New Order's survival, and so, she played both sides off against each other.<ref name="EGW" />

Nine months after Endor,<ref name="RSO3">''[[Star Wars Omnibus: X-Wing Rogue Squadron Volume 3]]''</ref> matters came to a head at [[Brentaal IV/Legends|Brentaal IV]], a key military and commercial hyperspace junction in the Core. Neither Pestage nor the Cabal wished to lose the world&mdash;the Grand Vizier sought to hold the planet for strategic reasons and to prove himself capable of resisting the New Republic,<ref name="RS22">[[X-Wing Rogue Squadron 22|''X-Wing Rogue Squadron'' 22]]</ref> while leading members of the ERC had important holdings there, and it was home to at least one councilor.<ref name="RS28" /> But Brentaal was defended by the incompetent Admiral [[Lon Isoto]], who Isard presented to the Grand Vizier as the Cabal's candidate, while persuading leading members of the Council that he was Pestage's man. As Isoto stumbled his way from disaster to defeat, Isard told each side that the other was preventing his replacement by a more competent commander, in the hope of undermining their position.<ref name="RS22" />

While the Grand Vizier was astute enough to realize that he had been manipulated by Isard, the Cabal blamed Pestage for his conduct of the war, and some began to openly suggest recruiting warlords such as [[Blitzer Harrsk]] and [[Treuten Teradoc]] to defend their holdings rather than rely on commanders loyal&mdash;as they thought&mdash;to the Grand Vizier.<ref name="RS28" /> Pestage's position was weakened by his loss of Sarcev Quest's support: the former Emperor's Hand believed that the real Grand Vizier had fled and replaced himself on Coruscant with a mentally unstable [[Cloning/Legends|clone]].<ref name="EP" />

[[File:Tribunemeeting.jpg|thumb|The Tribunal under General Paltr Carvin]]
As Pestage sought to escape Isard's machinations and secure his own control of his fiefdom in the [[Ciutric Hegemony]], Isard presented his actions to members of the Council as [[Treason/Legends|treason]] against the Empire, and called on them to act. With Pestage on the run, the tribunal&mdash;now composed of [[High General]] [[Paltr Carvin]],<ref name="RS32">[[X-Wing Rogue Squadron 32|''X-Wing Rogue Squadron'' 32]]</ref> the Council's elected leader and commander in the [[Coruscant Defense Forces]] ,<ref name="CSWEIRC">{{CSWECite|II|95|Imperial Ruling Council}}</ref> alongside [[Tribune]]s [[Challer]]<ref name="RS33">[[X-Wing Rogue Squadron 33|''X-Wing Rogue Squadron'' 33]]</ref> and [[Plumba]]&mdash;seized power, although they were rapidly deposed in turn by Isard herself.<ref name="RS35">[[X-Wing Rogue Squadron 35|''X-Wing Rogue Squadron'' 35]]</ref> Her remaining opponents eliminated, Isard established a dictatorship with herself as Empress in all but name, including a personal escort of the [[Emperor's Royal Guard/Legends|Imperial Royal Guard]], while allowing the Ruling Council to persist as a powerless legislative body.<ref name="EGW" />

===After the fall of Coruscant===
[[File:Orinda.jpg|thumb|left|250px|The fall of Coruscant allowed the Ruling Council to return to power on Orinda.]]
After Isard's [[Liberation of Coruscant (Galactic Civil War)|loss of Coruscant]] and her retreat to [[Thyferra/Legends|Thyferra]], Dangor and a reformed Ruling Council relocated to the Imperial-held trade world of [[Orinda/Legends|Orinda]], where they once again provided a central authority for the Empire, though their control over its bickering Moffs was tenuous.<ref name="EGW" /> They supported [[Grand Admiral/Legends|Grand Admiral]] [[Mitth'raw'nuruodo/Legends|Thrawn]] as Supreme Commander&mdash;mistakenly believing that as an alien, and with no standing in their rarified political world, he would necessarily remain beholden to their patronage and government. They considered granting him the title of Emperor if he was successful, still assuming they could control him afterwards;<ref name="DESB" /> however, even during his campaign he acted largely on his own, stating that he was the sole leader of the Empire.<ref name="DFR">''[[Dark Force Rising]]''</ref>

At this time, [[New Republic Council Research]] uncovered rumors of the Imperial Ruling Council's existence and preparations for war; but its director, [[Voren Na'al/Legends|Voren Na'al]], was unable to substantiate them and doubted their probability.<ref name="DFRSB">''[[Dark Force Rising Sourcebook]]''</ref> Though Orinda fell to the New Republic in the aftermath of Thrawn's death, the Ruling Council were able to build on his successes by driving the Republic from the Core and [[Second Battle of Coruscant|reconquering Coruscant]]<ref name="EGW" /> under the clandestine direction of a reborn Emperor Palpatine, resurrected in a clone body.<ref name="EA" />

[[File:Monument_Plaza_Mutiny.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Under Ars Dangor's Ruling Circle, the Empire fell into civil war.]]
Ars Dangor's suggestion that a new ruler be elected<ref name="DESB" /> provoked disagreement between the Ruling Council and Moffs on how to proceed, and escalated into a vicious [[Imperial Civil War|civil war]] with the [[Imperial Navy/Legends|Navy]], [[Inquisitorius/Legends|Inquisitorius]], COMPNOR, and Imperial Security Bureau.<ref name="EGW" /> Within the Council itself, Sarcev Quest had been building up support among his fellow Advisors and units of the Imperial Royal Guard to advocate for the leadership of [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]] Guardsman [[Carnor Jax]],<ref name="EP" /> Quest's student in the dark side who had been tasked with infiltrating the Imperial leadership by his [[Sith Master/Legends|master]], [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lady of the Sith]] [[Lumiya]]. Their machinations were interrupted by the reappearance of Palpatine,<ref name="END">{{Hyperspace|url=hyperspace/member/insideronline/88/indexp2.html|text=''Evil Never Dies: The Sith Dynasties''|int=Evil Never Dies: The Sith Dynasties}}</ref> who made his survival known to [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] and assembled a new [[Dark Empire]] from the [[Deep Core/Legends|Deep Core]] [[Safe world/Legends|safeworld]] of [[Byss/Legends|Byss]] in [[10 ABY/Legends|10 ABY]].<ref name="EA" />

===The Council on Byss===
[[File:SedrissVersusNefta.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Executor Sedriss defended his Emperor from traitors among the Council.]]
Though he claimed loyalty to the reborn Emperor, Sarcev Quest was no longer Palpatine's loyal spy among the Advisors, and the Council members were reluctant to surrender the authority they had acquired since Endor&mdash;not even to Palpatine. At Quest's urging, the Council lent its patronage to Carnor Jax as a new figurehead for the Empire. Laying the groundwork for a coup, Quest installed Jax as one of the cadre of [[Imperial Sovereign Protector]]s who provided Palpatine's personal guard, and, with funds provided by Imperial Ruling Council members, bribed the [[Emperor's physician]] to sabotage the genetic material for the clone bodies which were the key to Palpatine's rebirth. At the same time, Quest's rival dark side councilors [[Nefta]] and [[Sa-Di]]<ref name="EP" /> struck openly against the Emperor's clone reserves, only to be [[Skirmish on Byss|slain]] by the loyalist [[Executor (Imperial rank)|Executor]] [[Sedriss QL|Sedriss]].<ref name="DEII2">[[Dark Empire II 1|''Dark Empire II'' 1]]</ref>

Narrowly avoiding exposure by Council members hoping to curry favor with the Emperor,<ref name="SWH2" /> Quest's conspiracy bore fruit, and he and Jax seized control<ref name="EP" /> when the Dark Empire was struck a deathblow with the simultaneous [[destruction of Byss]] by the misfiring of the Imperial [[Galaxy Gun]] [[Superweapon/Legends|superweapon]] and [[Battle of Onderon (Galactic Civil War)|death of Palpatine's final clone]] on [[Onderon/Legends|Onderon]],<ref name="EE2">[[Empire's End 2|''Empire's End'' 2]]</ref>

===The "Council of Blood"===
{{Quote|Those on the Council will be the next to die&hellip; after ''you''!|Kir Kanos, to Carnor Jax|<ref name="CE6" />}}
[[File:IIRC.jpg|thumb|250px|The Interim Ruling Council in session on Ord Cantrell]]

With the destruction of the Emperor and original Ruling Council,<ref name="CSWEIIRC">{{CSWECite|II|91|Imperial Interim Ruling Council}}</ref> Carnor Jax's confederates formed the Imperial Interim Ruling Council to fill the void in their [[Lord/Legends|Lord's]] [[Crimson Empire]], including, for the first time, [[Non-huMan|non-human]] members.<ref name="EA" /> Lord Jax used his control over the Ruling Council in a bid to assume Palpatine's position,<ref name="CE1">[[Crimson Empire 1|''Crimson Empire'' 1]]</ref> but found his ambitions under threat from the Imperial Royal Guard, who had discovered his part in the death of the Emperor. Jax had them [[Attack on the Imperial Royal Guard Academy|slaughtered]], but a sole survivor, [[Kir Kanos]], escaped<ref name="CE0">[[Crimson Empire 0|''Crimson Empire'' 0]]</ref> with knowledge that could bring down both Jax and the Ruling Council.<ref name="CE2">[[Crimson Empire 2|''Crimson Empire'' 2]]</ref> Hunting Kanos on the planets [[Zaadja/Legends|Zaadja]], [[Phaeda/Legends|Phaeda]],<ref name="CE1" /> and finally [[Yinchorr/Legends|Yinchorr]], Jax instead [[Duel in The Squall|met his end]] at Kanos' hand in [[The Squall/Legends|the Squall]], the Guardsman's arena where they had once trained alongside each other.<ref name="CE6" /> The Council quickly turned on Quest, now stripped of Jax's protection, subjecting him to a week of [[Torture/Legends|torture]] before abandoning him on [[Nar Shaddaa/Legends|Nar Shadaa]],<ref name="EP" /> the [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggler's]] [[Moon/Legends|moon]].<ref name="EA" />

The Imperial Interim Ruling Council hastily convened at a [[Council Tower|tower headquarters]] in the [[De-Purteen]] resort on the the planet [[Ord Cantrell/Legends|Ord Cantrell]]. In reaction to the deaths of Jax and General<ref name="CEII1">[[Crimson Empire II: Council of Blood 1|''Crimson Empire II: Council of Blood'' 1]]</ref> [[Redd Wessel]], his military director, Councilman [[Burr Nolyds]] became the body's acting head, though his tenure was brief.<ref name="SWH2" /> [[Nom Anor]], a representative of the [[extragalactic]] [[Yuuzhan Vong]] who had once sought an alliance with Jax,<ref name="EP" /> had instead joined Council member [[Xandel Carivus]] in a plot to usurp Nolyds' leadership. When the acting head was killed in [[Burr Nolyds's chambers|his quarters]] by a [[Self-destruct mechanism/Legends|self-destructing]] [[message disk]], the Ruling Council elected Carivus in his place, believing him to be easily manipulated and an likely target for assassination.<ref name="CEII1" /> Framing Kanos, Jax's killer, for the deaths, Anor's next victim among the Council was Admiral<ref name="SWH2" /> [[Llon Banjeer]].<ref name="EGW" /> In reality, the Yuuzhan Vong spy had been tasked with hastening the downfall of the Empire, destabilizing the [[Galaxy/Legends|galaxy]], and paving the way for his kind's [[Yuuzhan Vong War|coming invasion]].<ref name="NEGC">''[[The New Essential Guide to Characters]]''</ref>

[[File:Imp_Interim_Ruling_Council.jpg|thumb|left|140px|The Imperial Interim Ruling Council members]]

However, Anor and Carivus were not the only force manipulating the Interim Ruling Council: [[Feena D'Asta]], who had taken the Council seat of her ailing father,<ref name="CEII5">[[Crimson Empire II: Council of Blood 5|''Crimson Empire II: Council of Blood'' 5]]</ref> vehicle manufacturer [[Baron/Legends|Baron]] [[Ragez D'Asta]], had been abducted by the crime syndicate [[Black Sun/Legends|Black Sun]] and replaced with a [[Feena D'Asta (clone)|clone]] [[7 ABY/Legends|four years prior]]. Acting as their agent on the Council, she advanced their agenda of peace between the Empire and the New Republic. The next death on the Council, that of General [[Immodet]],<ref name="SWH2" /> was orchestrated by the Black Sun<ref name="YA">{{DB|character|yullacib|Acib, Y'ull}}</ref> and prompted a paranoid Carivus to appoint his own [[Xandel Carivus's Private Guard|private guard]] as internal security. Carivus' guard arrested his rival the clone D'Asta and all non-human Councilors, killing [[Spearmaster]] [[Ch'Unkk]] when the [[Whiphid/Legends|Whiphid]] attempted to resist.<ref name="CEII3">[[Crimson Empire II: Council of Blood 3|''Crimson Empire II: Council of Blood'' 3]]</ref> Black Sun's conspiracy was revealed to the Council following an unsuccessful attempt to substitute Carivus himself for a [[Xandel Carivus (clone)|clone]], adding to the threats posed by the New Republic, potential reprisal from forces loyal to D'Asta and Ch'Unkk, and Carivus' falsified attacks by Kanos, and generating concern among the remaining Councilors. In turn, Carivus dismissed the services of Nom Anor and declared himself Emperor, disbanding<ref name="CEII5" /> and jailing the Council.<ref name="CEII6">[[Crimson Empire II: Council of Blood 6|''Crimson Empire II: Council of Blood'' 6]]</ref>

Emperor Carivus stood alone against Baron D'Asta, who launched an [[Battle of Ord Cantrell|assault]] on Ord Cantrell in retribution for his daughter's imprisonment. With his Empire's forces spread too thin, Carivus released the clone Feena in exchange for a cease of hostilities. However, the Baron was also contacted by New Republic [[Commander/Legends|Commander]] [[Mirith Sinn]], who had [[Attack on Grappa the Hutt's fortress|liberated]] the genuine Feena D'Asta and Kir Kanos from the [[Grappa's palace|palace]] of Black Sun-affiliate [[Grappa (Hutt)|Grappa]] the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]]. Though Kanos sought the death of the clone for her unwilling role in the assassination of Palpatine, Sinn redirected his attentions to Carivus. Using a private audience between the Baron and Emperor as cover, Kanos slew Carivus, though he spared the former Councilors he had held prisoner.<ref name="CEII6" /> After less than a [[Standard year/Legends|year]], the Crimson Empire had collapsed, taking with it the Imperial Ruling Council and the last vestiges of centralized Imperial control.<ref name="EA" />

===Aftermath===
In [[13 ABY/Legends|13 ABY]], surviving Councilors Ragez and Feena D'Asta allied themselves with the [[Imperial Remnant/Legends|Imperial Remnant]],<ref name="CEIII2">[[Crimson Empire III: Empire Lost 2|''Crimson Empire III: Empire Lost'' 2]]</ref> a confederation of former [[Warlord/Legends|warlord]] holdings under the leadership of Grand Admiral Thrawn's protegé Admiral [[Gilad Pellaeon/Legends|Gilad Pellaeon]] and governed by the [[Council of Moffs/Legends|Council of Moffs]].<ref name="EA" /> Opposing the Moffs, the D'Astas pushed Pellaeon towards peace with the New Republic, a stance that resulted in Feena's death at the hands of a [[Restored Empire|faction of Imperial hardliners]].<ref name="CEIII5">[[Crimson Empire III: Empire Lost 5|''Crimson Empire III: Empire Lost'' 5]]</ref>

Following his betrayal by and ejection from the Imperial Ruling Council, Sarcev Quest went into hiding, making his way from Nar Shadaa to the Core, where he paid for passage aboard a [[Luxury liner/Legends|luxury liner]] to seek refuge in the [[Corporate Sector/Legends|Corporate Sector]]. However, Quest was subject to a [[Bounty/Legends|price]] placed on his head by [[Jeng Droga]], another former Emperor's Hand,<ref name="EP" /> and he was captured by [[Ailyn Vel]], [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] and estranged daughter of the legendary [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] [[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba Fett]]. Taking vengeance on the traitorous Quest,<ref name="HM">{{InsiderCite|80|The History of the Mandalorians: Exploring the Evolution of a Mighty Race of Warriors}}</ref> Droga executed his one-time fellow in [[23 ABY/Legends|23 ABY]].<ref name="EGF">[[Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force (real-life book)|''Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force'']]</ref>

==Organization and duties==
The Emperor's Inner Circle served as advisors to Palpatine. Its members, several of whom were [[Human/Legends|human]] [[Gender/Legends|males]] with pale skin and sunken features, wore [[Color/Legends|purple-]] and burgundy-colored robes and elaborate headwear. Many of the Circle's number played significant roles in the Imperial bureaucracy,<ref name="AJC" /> particularly Sate Pestage<ref name="DESB" /> and Ars Dangor, who each found much of the day-to-day management of the Empire in their hands.<ref name="DSTC" /> On the fortress world Byss, the Emperor and the [[darksider]]s of his inner circle developed the immense subservient clone warriors known as [[Imperial Sentinel]]s, while in the wider galaxy the inner circle relied on trusted agents such as [[Wullf Yularen/Legends|Wullf Yularen]] of the Imperial Security Bureau.<ref name="FUCG" /> The advisors of the inner circle<ref name="AJC" /> were disdained by the Emperor's apprentice Darth Vader as self-important and petty, preoccupied with enriching themselves and gaining prestige.<ref name="ROTJn" /> Initially, Palpatine's inner circle included Sly Moore and Mas Amedda,<ref name="DLRODV" /> [[Alien/Legends|aliens]] who had served him in his Republic office.<ref name="AOTC" /> However, [[humanocentrism]] was pervasive in the Empire, and the Imperial Council would not include alien members until the Emperor's final death<ref name="EA" /> in [[11 ABY/Legends|11 ABY]].<ref name="NEC" />

Led by Pestage as Grand Vizier,<ref name="EGW" /> the Imperial Council was responsible for the live broadcast of [[Holodocumentary|holodocumentaries]] such as ''[[Life on Tatooine]]'', aired during the [[Blockade of Kashyyyk (1 ABY)|blockade]] of the [[Wookiee/Legends|Wookiee]] planet [[Kashyyyk/Legends|Kashyyyk]] and conceived to reinforce the loyalty of the Imperial citizenry through comparison of their own lives to the suffering of others.<ref name="HS">''[[The Star Wars Holiday Special]]''</ref> Prior to his defeat at Endor, many of Palpatine's [[Dark side adept/Legends|Dark Side Adepts]] were inducted into the Imperial Ruling Council, a move towards the Emperor's vision of a Dark Side [[Theocracy]] taking the place of the Empire's secular bureaucrats.<ref name="DESB" /> Imperial [[Captain/Legends|captain]] [[Zeta Traal]]<ref name="VRR">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/sw20030306velmor|text=Velmor: Royalty and Rebellion|int=Velmor: Royalty and Rebellion}}</ref> sought to be rewarded with a seat on the Council for her capture of the Rebel [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] aspirant [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]].<ref name="SW49">[[Star Wars (1977) 49|''Star Wars'' (1977) 49]]</ref>

With Palpatine's death at Endor, the Imperial Ruling Council rose to power over the remnants of his dominion, struggling to restore its control over the galaxy.<ref name="CSWEIRC" /> The members of this Council were internally addressed as tribunes, and as lords by even highly-placed Imperial outsiders.<ref name="RS33" /> While Pestage took the throne, his rivals formed the Emperor's Ruling Circle,<ref name="NEC" /> a significant force under Dangor's leadership.<ref name="CTD" /> The Imperial Ruling Council's power was sapped by Pestage's successor Ysanne Isard, but regained some of its authority when it was resurrected under Dangor on Orinda after her fall, which he invested in Grand Admiral Thrawn, and would later allow his Council to retake Coruscant<ref name="EGW" /> and subsequently call for the election of a new Emperor from their number.<ref name="DESB" />

[[File:SWCEIICOB1-FC.jpg|thumb|right|250px|The Imperial Ruling Council included alien members for the first time under the Crimson Empire.]]
When he took the throne, Lord Carnor Jax assembled the military, political, and economic figures who had been his co-conspirators and benefactors into the Imperial Interim Ruling Council, including the [[Noble/Legends|aristocratic]] Burr Nolyds, conniving bureaucrat Xandel Carivus, callous tactician Admiral [[Jeratai]], media mogul [[Mahd Windcaller]], and [[Tann Starpyre]], representative of the [[Diet of Imperial Planetary Governors]] who maintained a veneer of [[Democracy/Legends|democracy]] within the Empire. The presence of non-humans, such as the Whiphid [[clan]] leader Ch'Unkk, [[Devaronian/Legends|Devaronian]] [[Union (workers)|union]]-lord [[Manos]], [[Myke]] warlord [[Norym Kim]], [[Defel/Legends|Defel]] [[Prince/Legends|Prince]] [[Za]], and the [[Givin/Legends|Givin]] [[Kooloota-Fyf]] of the [[Shipbuilders and Astromechs Guild]], granted status on the Council to ensure the cooperation of their constituents, created internal friction with more traditionalist Councilors. The false Feena D'Asta spoke for her supposed father, ailing Ragez D'Asta of the [[D'Astan sector]] and [[D'Asta private fleet|private fleet]], while the [[Imperial Army/Legends|Imperial Army]] and Navy had presence on the Council in the persons, respectively, of General Immodet and Admiral Banjeer.<ref name="SWH2" /> Sarcev Quest abused Jax's protection to reign in tyranny over his fellow councilors, striking against any potential rivals among them.<ref name="EP" />

==Behind the scenes==
The Imperial Ruling council was first mentioned as the "Imperial Council" in [[1978]]'s ''[[The Star Wars Holiday Special]]'',<ref name="HS" /> and made their first appearance in [[James Kahn]]'s [[1983]] [[Star Wars: Return of the Jedi (novelization)|novelization]] of [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Star Wars'': Episode VI ''Return of the Jedi'']].<ref name="ROTJn" />

The name "Emperor's Ruling Circle" was first used in the [[1991]] [[Dark Empire 1|first issue]] of [[Dark Horse Comics|Dark Horse]] [[Star Wars comic books|comic book]] series [[Star Wars: Dark Empire|''Dark Empire'']],<ref name="DE1">[[Dark Empire 1|''Dark Empire'' 1]]</ref> and "Imperial Ruling Council" in [[West End Games]]' [[1992]] ''[[Dark Force Rising Sourcebook]]''.<ref name="DFRSB" /> Though the Ruling Council was described only as a pre-Battle of Endor entity, in contrast to the post-Endor Ruling Circle,<ref name="DESB" /> Dark Horse's [[1997]] comic [[Crimson Empire 1|''Crimson Empire'' 1]] introduced a later incarnation of the Ruling Council,<ref name="CE1" /> and the article ''[[The Emperor's Pawns]]'' of the [[2001]] magazine [[Star Wars Gamer 5|''Star Wars Gamer'' 5]] equated the three groups.<ref name="EP" />

The Imperial Interim Ruling Council's numbers have been depicted inconsistently between various sources. In the [[Star Wars: Crimson Empire (series)|''Crimson Empire'' series of comics]], the Council is shown to have thirteen members both human and alien,<ref name="SWH2" /> with a fourteenth, Sarcev Quest, introduced in ''The Emperor's Pawns''.<ref name="EP" /> [[2008]]'s ''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]'' indicated that the body consisted of thirteen Imperial loyalists in addition to a further number of non-human councilors,<ref name="CSWEIIRC" /> while in [[2009]] ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' claimed that the Council had only twelve members.<ref name="EA" />
